title: Content Analysis of Korean Videos Regarding Restless Legs Syndrome on YouTube
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of 80 Korean-language YouTube videos on restless legs syndrome, each explicitly classified 'reliable' or 'misleading' by two neurologists (κ=0.90). Reports 36/80 (45.0%) misleading — a CONTENT prevalence share with an explicit denominator. A separate mDISCERN quality share is also reported and kept as a QUALITY row.

estimates.measure_type: % of Korean-language YouTube videos about restless legs syndrome classified as misleading
estimates.denominator: 80 Korean-language YouTube videos on restless legs syndrome — the first 100 results for the Korean-language query “restless legs syndrome” under the default relevance filter, minus 20 exclusions (11 unrelated, 2 patient experiences, 7 unavailable/soundless)
estimates.definition: Video containing inaccurate or scientifically unproven information about RLS (the complement, 'reliable', required correct scientific information and no inaccurate information)
estimates.misinfo_def: “misleading videos were defined as videos containing inaccurate or scientifically unproven information”
estimates.source_quote: Among the 80 videos analyzed, 44 (55.0%) were reliable, and 36 (45.0%) were misleading.
estimates.page_loc: Abstract, Results, p. 144; repeated in Results, p. 145 ('Among 80 videos, 44 (55.0%) were categorized as "reliable", and 36 (45.0%) were categorized as "misleading".')
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two neurologists (R.K. and J.S.J.) evaluated every video independently, blinded to each other's ratings; disagreements resolved by discussion. Interrater agreement for accuracy Cohen's κ = 0.90 ('excellent'); ICC = 0.80 for the mDISCERN quality scores.
estimates.moderator_quote: A YouTube (http://www.youtube.com) search was performed using the keyword “restless legs syndrome” in the Korean language on April 1, 2020, using the default filter of “relevance”. ... We screened the first 100 videos ... Finally, 80 videos were included in the analysis. ... The included videos were evaluated independently by two neurologists (R. K. and J. S. J.) who were blinded to each other’s ratings
estimates.notes: Judgement call worth an adjudicator's eye: the misleading label covers 'inaccurate OR scientifically unproven' information, and the authors' own third limitation concedes that 'some treatments may be classified as misleading because there is a lack of clinical trials and not because of their ineffectiveness'. Coded CONTENT rather than QUALITY because the coding is an explicit reliable/misleading accuracy judgement by domain experts against scientific evidence, and a wholly accurate video could not receive the label — but the numerator is broader than falsity, hence breadth=misleading. denom_selection=curated because the frame is the first 100 relevance-ranked search results (rank-truncated).

estimates.measure_type: % of 'reliable' RLS videos that were of low quality on the modified DISCERN instrument (mDISCERN < 3)
estimates.denominator: 44 Korean-language RLS YouTube videos classified as reliable
estimates.definition: Mean mDISCERN total score across the two raters below 3 on the 0–5 modified DISCERN scale
estimates.misinfo_def: “misleading videos were defined as videos containing inaccurate or scientifically unproven information”
estimates.page_loc: Results, p. 146 — full sentence, broken across a two-column line break in the text file: 'However, 21 (47.7%) reliable videos had low quality (mDISCERN score < 3).'
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two neurologists scored each video on the 5-item modified DISCERN instrument; the mean of the two raters' scores was used; ICC = 0.80. The authors note the <3 cutoff for 'low quality' has not been validated.
estimates.moderator_quote: We measured the quality of the videos using the modified DISCERN (mDISCERN) instrument,9 which is a 5 item scale adapted from the original 16 item DISCERN scale.10 ... The video quality was regarded as low if the mDISCERN score was less than 3.
estimates.notes: QUALITY construct per §3 (DISCERN score → QUALITY, excluded from prevalence). borderline=true because a wholly accurate video routinely scores <3 on mDISCERN — indeed this share is computed only among videos already judged accurate. Denominator is the reliable subset (44), not all 80.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) Within-misinformation theme breakdowns are not falsity shares and were not extracted: of the 36 misleading videos, 26 (72.2%) recommended complementary and alternative medicine, 11 (30.6%) oriental medicine, 9 (25.0%) acupuncture, 4 (11.1%) nasal breathing, 2 (5.6%) venesection, 1 (2.8%) aroma therapy; as primary etiology 10 (27.8%) advocated 'poor blood circulation', 4 (11.1%) 'constitution type', 1 (2.8%) 'oral breathing'. Table 1's per-domain 'misleading content' rows (epidemiology 1/2.8%, etiology 13/36.1%, symptoms 2/5.6%, treatment 26/72.2%) are likewise shares of the misleading videos describing WHERE the misinformation sat, not the prevalence of misinformation; extracting them would over-split the single 45.0% estimate. (2) mDISCERN mean scores (2.9 ± 1.0 reliable vs 1.3 ± 1.0 misleading) are means with no share, so no row per §3. (3) The '23% of the videos provided misleading information' figure in the Discussion is quoted from a different study of English-language RLS videos (ref 17) — excluded under R8. (4) Supplementary Table 1 high- vs low-quality comparisons are within the reliable subset and add no falsity share. (5) Viewership figures (cumulative views 101,139 reliable vs 77,720 misleading; mean daily views 2.2 vs 4.0) are engagement, not a share of consumption with a common denominator, so no EXPOSURE row is derivable without computing a cross-category ratio (barred by R8).

rob.design: Cross-sectional YouTube content analysis, single time point. Frame: first 100 results for the Korean-language term 'restless legs syndrome', default 'relevance' filter, browser history and cookies cleared before searching (1 April 2020); 20 excluded (11 unrelated to RLS, 2 patient experiences, 7 unavailable or soundless), leaving 80. No response rate (platform data). Two neurologists rated every video independently and blinded to each other, disagreements resolved by discussion; Cohen's κ = 0.90 for accuracy classification, ICC = 0.80 for mDISCERN. Stated limitations: single time point, results depend on default search settings, 'unproven' treatments may be labelled misleading for lack of trials, unvalidated mDISCERN cutoff, Korean-language only.
rob.item6_quote: The videos were classified as either “reliable” or “misleading.” Reliable videos were defined as videos containing correct scientific information about RLS and not containing any inaccurate information. On the other hand, misleading videos were defined as videos containing inaccurate or scientifically unproven information.
rob.item10_quote: Among 80 videos, 44 (55.0%) were categorized as “reliable”, and 36 (45.0%) were categorized as “misleading”.
